feedback: Iteration 0 is the only race so far, and every trial went off track with a single line-loss event and progress of 0.11 to 0.15. Max error reached about 0.06 m, which is the off-track limit for body_width 0.12 (max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.12/4)). So the robot leaves the line before it stalls, and the limit is the binding failure. Steering oscillation was highest on the slalom (0.153) and s-bend (0.143), and lowest on the oval (0.072). That points to oscillation tied to sharper features. Your iteration 1 narrowing to ±0.02 m at 10 mm spacing, with the row at y = 0.04, is a reasonable response to that pattern. I have built the controller for it: kp is reduced and kd raised so the steering gain stays near baseline on the narrower row. Hold this geometry for the next race so the controller is judged on it. Before the race reports anything, the one open question for the geometry is whether a row limited to ±0.02 m can still see the tape at the offsets where the robot leaves the line. Offsets beyond about 0.038 m would leave all sensors off tape, and that case would be line loss rather than steering.
requested_changes: Hold sensor_positions at x = -0.02 to 0.02 at y = 0.04 for the next race. If the result shows the single line-loss event at progress near 0 (start-up), the sensor reach is not the cause and the geometry should stay as it is.

If the next race still shows line loss after progress 0.1 on a bend, try sensor_size 0.016 with the same positions. The larger footprint keeps more tape visible at the row edges, which would show whether the loss is a coverage problem.

If the next race shows steering oscillation still above 0.1 on the slalom, try a forward offset of y = 0.02 to 0.03 with the same row. That would reduce the sensing lag further, which is the reason you gave for moving the row forward.
